context: A class of learners in which some play football, some play hockey, some play both sports and some play neither.
stem: A class has ${=t}$ learners. ${=f}$ of them play football and ${=h}$ of them play hockey, and ${=n}$ play neither football nor hockey. The numbers for football and for hockey each include the learners who play both. How many learners play both football and hockey?
solution: The ${=n}$ learners who play neither lie outside both circles, so the other ${=t} - {=n} = {=t - n}$ learners play football or hockey (or both): $n(F \text{ or } H) = {=t - n}$.
Use the identity $n(F \text{ or } H) = n(F) + n(H) - n(F \text{ and } H)$: ${=t - n} = {=f} + {=h} - n(F \text{ and } H)$.
So $n(F \text{ and } H) = {=f} + {=h} - {=t - n} = {=f + h - (t - n)}$ learners play both.
Check on the Venn diagram: football only ${=f} - {=c} = {=f - c}$, both ${=c}$, hockey only ${=h} - {=c} = {=h - c}$, neither ${=n}$, and ${=f - c} + {=c} + {=h - c} + {=n} = {=t}$.
notes: The twist on the book's ex14-8-30 (which gives the overlap and asks for the class total): here the total and the 'neither' count are given and the overlap is the unknown, so the union identity has to be rearranged. Three steps plus a check on the diagram. The inclusive reading of the football and hockey totals is stated in the stem. No distractors (numeric).
